newsitem.title: SPAIN: OLYMPICS-REJECTED SEVILLE VOWS TO TRY AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-REJECTED SEVILLE VOWS TO TRY AGAIN.

text.p: Leaders of Seville's bid to host the 2004 Olympics have vowed to try again after learning on Friday that their candidature was not among the five cities short-listed to host the Games.

"Sevilla brings together the conditions and should continue in the race. I believe possibly the nearness of Barcelona (host city in 1992) has been a determining factor," said mayoress Soledad Becerril.
The International Olympic Committee (IOC) will make its final choice between Athens, Buenos Aires, Cape Town, Rome and Stockholm on September 5.
Istanbul, Lille, Rio de Janeiro, San Juan, Seville and St Petersburg failed to make the cut.
While several other local politicians echoed Becerril's view, there was greater caution from Spanish national sporting authorities.

"The Spanish Olympic Committee must decide serenely to present a city again when it is known if there is more than one option," said Secretary of State for Sport Pedro Antonio Marin in an apparent reference to the possibility of Madrid also presenting a candidature.
Many people in Madrid felt slighted by the international attention given to the rival city of Barcelona in 1992.
Spanish Olympic Committee president Carlos Ferrer pointed out another possible problem posed by the presence of three European cities -- two of them Mediterranean -- in the final five.
"If Buenos Aires wins there are more possibilities than if Athens or Rome wins," he said.
